title: ARE multi-cycle evolution runtime
goal: Define a small ARE-native runtime in which agents use a JSON protocol while the runtime controls multiple independently defined evolution cycles and owns their state, generated data, evidence, accounting, receipts, recovery, and cross-cycle handoffs.
goal_limits: Benchmark-driven research is one cycle type and its semantic lifecycle is not the universal evolution model; historical E0 through E10 labels are migration aliases only.
The shared kernel owns generic state and evidence mechanics but does not invent cycle-specific transitions, success criteria, or authority.
Agents and workers propose commands and evidence; they cannot directly set persisted state, rewrite history, or claim a transition.
Generated data is runtime-managed and reconstructible, while credentials and other secrets are prohibited from persistence.
Cross-cycle reuse occurs through typed, receipt-bound handoffs rather than shared mutable state.
This pack does not authorize implementation, migration, provider calls, benchmark execution, activation, publication, release, or deployment.
original_intent: Create one durable ARE structure for evolution work so agents can interact through JSON, the runtime controls lifecycle state, receipts and all generated data remain organized and recoverable, and benchmark research remains separate from other evolution cycles.

context.name: ARE evolution coordination and evidence management
context.statement: The existing ARE evolution runtime already preserves improvement signals, research records, variants, comparisons, scheduling, and recommend-only upgrade decisions. The proposed successor separates a common coordination and evidence kernel from independently versioned cycle definitions. Benchmark research, research learning, engine improvement, interaction learning, and controlled upgrade become distinct cycle types connected only by typed handoffs.
context.provenance: User direction in the active Define session, the earlier ARE evolution-engine Definition Pack, the current evolution-runtime package, the ARE EvolutionCycle ontology node, the interaction-learning model, and the candidate-only GLM 8K benchmark workflow.

context_candidates.statement: The agent should interact only by submitting JSON while the runtime controls state.
Receipts and all generated benchmark and evolution data should be generated, organized, and recoverable inside the runtime boundary.
Benchmark research is one evolution cycle among several and must remain separately modeled.

context_sufficiency.requirement: The pack must distinguish the generic kernel, stored evidence, cycle definitions, cycle instances, cycle-specific policies, cross-cycle handoffs, agent and worker boundaries, and authority boundaries.
context_sufficiency.derivation: The explicit user constraints close the product boundary; current repository sources establish the predecessor runtime and known cycle semantics.
residue: The exact archive codec, pack format, operational root, and capacity thresholds require later implementation design.
The exact schemas for each cycle type require a later design and implementation route.
The exact validator implementations and five initial cycle-definition schemas require later design and implementation work.
The exact H-EN frontier import manifest and import implementation require later design and authorization.

goal_owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Agent Reasoning Engine product-meaning owner

consumer.intended_use: Meaning input for review of the multi-cycle evolution architecture and, only after separate authorization, a bounded implementation plan for the existing ARE evolution-runtime package.

definition.normative_voice: The ARE Multi-Cycle Evolution Runtime MUST accept bounded JSON commands, coordinate independently defined evolution cycles, own their durable state and evidence, and emit receipts without collapsing research evidence into authority.
definition.formal_voice: MultiCycleEvolutionRuntime = (EvolutionKernel, CycleDefinitionRegistry, ManagedEvidenceStore, ReceiptLedger, ProjectionService, AdapterBoundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: One small ARE service keeps every evolution workflow organized while allowing different kinds of evolution to follow different rules.
definition.domain_context_voice: It hosts benchmark research, research learning, engine improvement, interaction learning, and controlled upgrade as separate cycle types.
definition.boundary: It is not a single benchmark runner, a universal benchmark lifecycle, an autonomous code mutator, or an authority source.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine product-meaning owner plus evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: The Evolution Kernel MUST provide cycle identity, command validation, concurrency control, event recording, evidence ingestion, receipt generation, recovery, and definition-bound transition evaluation without embedding one cycle's domain states.
definition.formal_voice: EvolutionKernel(command, current_revision, cycle_definition, store) -> AcceptedEventAndProjection | RejectionReceipt.
definition.plain_language_voice: The kernel supplies the common machinery; each cycle definition supplies the workflow meaning.
definition.domain_context_voice: The kernel can host both a benchmark gate transition and an upgrade canary transition while treating their rules as different profiles.
definition.boundary: The kernel does not choose research hypotheses, benchmark thresholds, upgrade authorization, or terminal outcomes.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Program MUST group related cycle instances under one bounded improvement intent without merging their ledgers, state, budgets, or authority boundaries.
definition.formal_voice: EvolutionProgram = (program_id, intent, owner_ref, cycle_refs, shared_subject_refs, open_questions).
definition.plain_language_voice: A program is the umbrella for several related cycles, such as improving ARE context selection through research, engine changes, and later upgrade review.
definition.domain_context_voice: The GLM 8K ContextBench cycle and a later engine-improvement cycle may belong to one program while remaining independent cycle instances.
definition.boundary: A program is not an executable workflow and cannot transfer state or authority between its cycles.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine product owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Cycle Definition MUST immutably declare one cycle type's states, transition rules, required evidence, budgets, authority boundaries, terminal outcomes, and compatibility identity.
definition.formal_voice: CycleDefinition = (cycle_type, schema_version, definition_digest, states, transitions, evidence_requirements, budget_policy, authority_boundaries, terminal_outcomes).
definition.plain_language_voice: This is the versioned rulebook for one kind of evolution cycle.
definition.domain_context_voice: benchmark-research/v1 declares semantic commands, events, and states such as recover, recovery-confirmed, and awaiting-diagnosis, while controlled-upgrade/v1 declares its own authorization, activation, canary, retain, and rollback vocabulary.
definition.boundary: A definition is not a running cycle, permission to start work, or mutable configuration for an existing cycle.

concepts.decision_owner: User for admission; cycle-domain authors may only propose and validate candidates

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Cycle Instance MUST bind one immutable cycle definition to a subject, intent, owner, starting inputs, event chain, artifact inventory, budget accounts, and current derived state.
definition.formal_voice: CycleInstance = (cycle_id, definition_ref, definition_digest, subject_refs, intent, owner_ref, event_head, artifact_set, budget_accounts, projection_digest).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is one actual run of one cycle rulebook.
definition.domain_context_voice: glm8k-contextbench-hen-r1 is one benchmark-research instance; an upgrade review for a resulting variant would be a different instance.
definition.boundary: An instance cannot change its definition digest, inherit another instance's state, or imply that its work is authorized.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the exact cycle instance

definition.normative_voice: Cycle State MUST be the aggregate objective-level disposition deterministically derived from one cycle definition and its verified event chain; subordinate record and executable work states MUST be separate derived projections from that same authority chain, and callers MUST NOT set any layer directly.
definition.formal_voice: Projection_n = reduce(CycleDefinition, verified Events_0..n) = (CycleDisposition_n, RecordStates_n, WorkStates_n); direct assignment is invalid.
definition.plain_language_voice: The runtime separately calculates the overall cycle disposition, the status of each hypothesis or other record, and the readiness of each work item from one history.
definition.domain_context_voice: A benchmark cycle may remain active while one hypothesis is supported, another experiment is frozen, and several work items are ready or running.
definition.boundary: No projection is an independent authority, agent prose, a status-file edit, or evidence that a transition's real-world claim is true.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: A Transition Rule MUST name its source states, accepted command or event, required evidence and owner gates, guards, target state, rejection reasons, and emitted obligations.
definition.formal_voice: TransitionRule = (from, trigger, guards, evidence_predicate, owner_gate_refs, to, rejection_codes, emitted_obligations).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is the exact rule explaining when one cycle may move to its next state.
definition.domain_context_voice: A freeze transition can require a complete contract, exact source hashes, passing qualification, and an explicit launch-review record.
definition.boundary: A transition rule validates recorded inputs; it does not manufacture missing evidence or owner approval.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the cycle definition

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution JSON Command MUST carry a schema version, unique command identity, operation, cycle identity where applicable, expected revision, and operation-specific payload.
definition.formal_voice: JsonCommand = (schema_version, command_id, operation, cycle_id?, expected_revision?, payload).
definition.plain_language_voice: The agent asks the runtime to do one bounded thing using a versioned JSON message.
definition.domain_context_voice: Commands create or inspect a cycle, ingest an artifact, request a dispatch lease, settle work, record a decision, verify storage, or export reconstruction evidence.
definition.boundary: A command is a proposal, not proof, a state transition, a shell instruction, or authority.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Event MUST be an immutable, ordered record of one accepted state-relevant fact and MUST bind its predecessor, command, cycle definition, evidence, and resulting revision.
definition.formal_voice: EvolutionEvent = (event_id, cycle_id, revision, predecessor_digest, command_digest, definition_digest, event_kind, payload_digest, evidence_refs, event_digest).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is the permanent fact the runtime accepted into a cycle's history.
definition.domain_context_voice: artifact-ingested, lease-issued, work-settled, gate-passed, and decision-recorded are different event kinds.
definition.boundary: Rejected commands and disposable query responses do not become state-changing events.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Receipt MUST report the bounded result of every command, accepted or rejected, and bind command identity, cycle and definition identity, state and budget before and after, evidence digests, reason codes, predecessor receipt, runtime version, and authority effect.
definition.formal_voice: EvolutionReceipt = (receipt_id, command_digest, disposition, cycle_ref?, definition_digest?, before_digest?, after_digest?, budget_before?, budget_after?, evidence_refs, reason_codes, predecessor_receipt_digest?, runtime_version, authority_effect, receipt_digest).
definition.plain_language_voice: The receipt explains exactly what the runtime accepted or refused and what changed.
definition.domain_context_voice: A rejected dispatch request still receives a receipt showing the unmet gate or exhausted budget.
definition.boundary: A receipt proves only the recorded runtime decision; it does not prove external truth, owner authority, model quality, or downstream effects.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner plus governance-model owner

definition.normative_voice: The Managed Evolution Evidence Store MUST durably ingest, identify, classify, relate, verify, retrieve, archive, restore, and export all cycle-generated non-secret data and receipts under runtime control while minimizing duplicate and hot-storage bytes.
definition.formal_voice: ManagedEvidenceStore = (HotMetadata, GlobalContentAddressedObjects, WarmCompressedObjects, ColdVerifiedArchives, ArtifactCatalog, ReceiptLedger, EventLedger, ProjectionBuilder, VerificationRestoreAndExport).
definition.plain_language_voice: The runtime, not the agent, organizes all experiment history and moves old heavy evidence into compact verified archives.
definition.domain_context_voice: Small manifests, receipts, hashes, accounting, and decisions remain hot; raw prompts, responses, logs, fixtures, and intermediate outputs may move from compressed shared storage into verified cold packs.
definition.boundary: Logical runtime ownership does not require storing large bytes in SQLite; archive is not deletion; credentials or secrets must never enter the store.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Evidence Artifact MUST be immutable bytes identified by digest, size, media type, classification, producer, ingestion receipt, and claim ceiling.
definition.formal_voice: EvidenceArtifact = (artifact_digest, byte_length, media_type, classification, producer_ref, ingestion_receipt_ref, claim_ceiling).
definition.plain_language_voice: Any file or structured result becomes stable evidence only after the runtime hashes and ingests it.
definition.domain_context_voice: A raw model response, TAP log, review JSON, score summary, or frozen contract can each be an artifact.
definition.boundary: An artifact's existence does not make its contents true, sufficient, current, or authorized.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the producing cycle plus evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: A Cycle Artifact Binding MUST connect one immutable artifact to its cycle, gate or state, attempt, producer, role, semantic validator, and admissibility result without changing the artifact bytes.
definition.formal_voice: ArtifactBinding = (binding_id, artifact_digest, cycle_id, state_ref, attempt_ref?, producer_ref, role, validator_ref?, admissibility).
definition.plain_language_voice: The same stored bytes can be referenced safely while their meaning remains specific to one cycle and purpose.
definition.domain_context_voice: A test log may support construction validation in one cycle and remain merely contextual evidence in another.
definition.boundary: Global byte deduplication never implies global semantic reuse or cross-cycle admission.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the receiving cycle

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution State Projection MUST be reproducible from a cycle definition and verified events and MUST expose the aggregate cycle disposition, subordinate record states, executable work states, blockers, evidence inventory, accounting, and next admissible operations.
definition.formal_voice: StateProjection = project(definition_digest, verified_event_chain, verified_artifact_bindings) = (cycle, records, work, blockers, evidence, accounting, next_operations).
definition.plain_language_voice: This is the current layered readable view rebuilt from one durable history.
definition.domain_context_voice: cycle.inspect can show an active H-EN objective, one hypothesis awaiting validation, its review work item ready, and its bound R2 evidence; E5 remains only a legacy alias.
definition.boundary: A projection is disposable and cannot replace the event chain or artifact store.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: The SQLite Evolution Operational Index MUST transactionally coordinate queries, uniqueness checks, revision control, budgets, and active leases while remaining rebuildable from durable events, receipts, artifacts, and archive manifests.
definition.formal_voice: SQLiteOperationalIndex = rebuild(EventLedger, ReceiptLedger, ArtifactCatalog, ArchiveManifests); loss(SQLiteOperationalIndex) != loss(Evidence).
definition.plain_language_voice: SQLite coordinates live work, but compact immutable evidence remains the recoverable history.
definition.domain_context_voice: SQLite prevents double dispatch across two workers while archived receipts and objects preserve cycle reconstruction.
definition.boundary: An index is not canonical evidence and cannot create provenance that is missing from the ledgers.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Work Item MUST describe one cycle-defined unit of external or local work with prerequisites, input artifact bindings, expected outputs, budget reservation, worker contract, and settlement conditions.
definition.formal_voice: WorkItem = (work_id, cycle_id, state_ref, prerequisite_refs, input_bindings, expected_output_roles, budget_reservation, worker_contract_ref, settlement_policy).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is a precise piece of work the runtime may make available to a worker.
definition.domain_context_voice: One ContextBench task execution or one independent construction review can be represented as a work item.
definition.boundary: A work item is not permission to execute until a valid lease is issued.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the cycle definition

definition.normative_voice: A Dispatch Lease MUST reserve one work item, worker identity, bounded resources, budget, expiry, and concurrency slot only after all cycle guards and authority requirements pass.
definition.formal_voice: DispatchLease = (lease_id, work_id, worker_ref, reserved_budget, concurrency_slot, issued_revision, expires_at, settlement_requirement).
definition.plain_language_voice: The runtime gives one worker a temporary, bounded claim on one piece of work.
definition.domain_context_voice: At most two model workers may hold live leases in the current GLM 8K benchmark contract.
definition.boundary: A lease does not prove the work ran, succeeded, or stayed within budget; settlement records those facts.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the cycle instance plus exact effect owner where external calls are involved

definition.normative_voice: A Work Settlement MUST close or explicitly fail one dispatch lease by recording terminal worker status, every output and failure artifact, actual accounting, unresolved usage, and post-settlement verification.
definition.formal_voice: WorkSettlement = (settlement_id, lease_ref, terminal_status, output_bindings, failure_bindings, actual_usage, unknown_usage, verification_result).
definition.plain_language_voice: It closes the books on a dispatched job, including failures and unknown costs.
definition.domain_context_voice: A model timeout still settles with request, error, known token usage, retry count, and any unknown provider usage preserved.
definition.boundary: Settlement means the dispatch is accounted for, not that its scientific or product objective succeeded.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Budget Account MUST track declared limits, reservations, settled consumption, failures, retries, unknown usage, and remaining capacity for one cycle-defined resource.
definition.formal_voice: BudgetAccount = (account_id, resource_kind, limit, reserved, settled, failed, unknown, remaining_or_unknown).
definition.plain_language_voice: It ensures calls, tokens, time, money, or attempts are counted even when work fails.
definition.domain_context_voice: The GLM 8K cycle tracks per-task and campaign model-call and model-token ceilings.
definition.boundary: Unknown usage remains unknown and cannot be converted to zero or estimated silently.

concepts.decision_owner: Owner of the cycle contract

definition.normative_voice: A Cycle Adapter MUST translate one external benchmark, evaluator, reviewer, or operational interface into declared commands and artifact roles without owning cycle state or bypassing kernel validation.
definition.formal_voice: CycleAdapter(external_input, adapter_contract) -> JsonCommand | StagedArtifactManifest.
definition.plain_language_voice: An adapter lets a particular benchmark speak the runtime's protocol.
definition.domain_context_voice: ContextBench, ARE-DSH, and a third benchmark use separate adapters under the same benchmark-research cycle definition.
definition.boundary: An adapter cannot set state, approve a gate, hide failures, or redefine the cycle.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine implementation owner plus benchmark or system owner

definition.normative_voice: A Cycle Worker MUST execute only the work described by a valid dispatch lease, write outputs to runtime-controlled staging, and settle or expire without directly mutating cycle state or durable evidence.
definition.formal_voice: CycleWorker(DispatchLease, InputBindings) -> StagedOutputs + SettlementCommand.
definition.plain_language_voice: The worker performs the job; the runtime decides what the result means for the cycle.
definition.domain_context_voice: A model runner, scorer, construction test process, or independent review tool can be a worker.
definition.boundary: A worker is not the state coordinator, evidence store, owner gate, or upgrade controller.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine implementation owner

definition.normative_voice: A Cross-Cycle Handoff MUST bind a typed output from one terminal or eligible source-cycle state to explicit artifacts, receipts, claim ceiling, intended receiving cycle type, and receiving acceptance status.
definition.formal_voice: CrossCycleHandoff = (handoff_id, source_cycle_ref, source_state_digest, output_type, artifact_bindings, receipt_refs, claim_ceiling, target_cycle_type, acceptance_status).
definition.plain_language_voice: One cycle can offer evidence to another, but the receiving cycle must inspect and accept it for its own purpose.
definition.domain_context_voice: A benchmark finding may become an input to engine improvement; an upgrade recommendation may become an input to controlled upgrade.
definition.boundary: A handoff never changes the receiving cycle automatically or transfers the source cycle's authority.

concepts.decision_owner: Owners of both source and receiving cycle definitions

definition.normative_voice: An Evolution Reconstruction Bundle MUST contain or content-address every definition, event, receipt, artifact binding, accounting record, decision, and verification result needed to reproduce one cycle's state without its disposable operational index.
definition.formal_voice: ReconstructionBundle = closure(cycle_definition, cycle_events, receipts, artifact_bindings, budget_records, terminal_decisions, verification_manifest).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is the portable evidence package needed to rebuild and audit a cycle.
definition.domain_context_voice: A completed benchmark campaign can be exported with raw requests and responses, scores, costs, reviews, freezes, and the final decision.
definition.boundary: A bundle preserves recorded evidence; it does not replay provider calls or certify conclusions independently.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: A Legacy Evolution Import MUST ingest existing artifacts with original identity, path, bytes, chronology posture, and limitations while marking retrospective records as imported rather than newly prospective evidence.
definition.formal_voice: LegacyImport(source_manifest, source_artifacts, import_policy) -> ImportedArtifactBindings + ImportReceipt; historical_posture is preserved.
definition.plain_language_voice: Old benchmark work can enter the runtime without pretending it was originally run there.
definition.domain_context_voice: The current H-EN repair evidence and rounds 73-78 can be imported with their existing hashes and correct benchmark classification.
definition.boundary: Import cannot refresh historical hashes, manufacture missing receipts, change exposed data into holdout data, or rewrite chronology.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine research owner plus evolution runtime owner

definition.normative_voice: A Benchmark Improvement Objective MUST immutably bind the feature or capability being improved, the desired goal, the benchmark and cohort, a typed metric policy with an explicit prospective decision rule, the observed baseline, success and falsification conditions, and applicable resource, quality, leakage, and operating constraints before its benchmark-research lifecycle begins. The metric policy MUST classify every measure as primary, guardrail, or diagnostic; only primary metrics determine success, every guardrail can block success under its frozen threshold, and diagnostic metrics can explain but cannot alter the decision.
definition.formal_voice: BenchmarkImprovementObjective = (objective_id, subject_feature, goal, benchmark_ref, cohort_ref, metric_policy(primary_metrics, guardrails, diagnostics, prospective_decision_rule), baseline_evidence, success_rule, falsification_rule, constraints, objective_digest).
definition.plain_language_voice: The objective says exactly what we are trying to improve and how the benchmark will decide whether it improved.
definition.domain_context_voice: An objective may target ARE context selection within an 8K request window using prospectively chosen ContextBench metrics and constraints; H-EN and H-MC are candidate hypotheses evaluated for that objective rather than the objective itself.
definition.boundary: A candidate, technique, execution result, or later metric change is not the objective. A material change to the objective creates a linked successor cycle instead of rewriting the admitted objective.

concepts.decision_owner: User for objective admission; Agent Reasoning Engine research owner may propose objective candidates

definition.normative_voice: A Benchmark Hypothesis MUST state one falsifiable explanation or proposed mechanism for completing an immutable Benchmark Improvement Objective and MUST preserve its own status, evidence, candidate implementations, experiments, attempts, accounting, exposure posture, and outcome within the cycle.
definition.formal_voice: BenchmarkHypothesis = (hypothesis_id, objective_ref, claim, mechanism, falsifier, status, candidate_refs, experiment_refs, attempt_refs, artifact_bindings, budget_usage, exposure_posture, outcome?).
definition.plain_language_voice: A hypothesis is one possible explanation or approach the cycle can explore to achieve its objective.
definition.domain_context_voice: H-EN and H-MC can be separate hypotheses under one ARE context-selection objective; each may produce one or more implementations and experiments before being supported, revised, rejected, or exhausted.
definition.boundary: A hypothesis is not a child cycle and cannot change the objective. Its evidence and accounting remain attributable, and evidence reuse across hypotheses must preserve explicit provenance and exposure posture.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine research owner within the user-admitted benchmark objective

definition.normative_voice: A Benchmark Research Cycle MUST bind one immutable Benchmark Improvement Objective and iteratively register and evaluate as many admissible Benchmark Hypotheses as are useful within its declared resource and safety bounds. Hypotheses may yield multiple candidate implementations, experiments, and attempts, but all remain records within the one objective lifecycle.
definition.formal_voice: BenchmarkResearchCycle/v1 = ImmutableObjective + Diagnosis + HypothesisPortfolio{0..n} + CandidateAndExperimentRecords + ObjectiveDecision.
definition.plain_language_voice: One cycle keeps trying evidence-backed hypotheses until it completes the objective or reaches an explicit stopping condition.
definition.domain_context_voice: An ARE context-selection objective can evaluate H-EN and H-MC as candidate hypotheses; ARE-DSH and other benchmarks use adapters rather than separate state machinery when they measure the same admitted objective.
definition.boundary: Candidate hypotheses and bounded attempts may change inside the cycle, but its feature, goal, benchmark scope, metric policy, baseline, success rule, falsification rule, and constraints cannot. A material objective change or untouched confirmation creates a linked successor cycle. A benchmark decision remains research evidence and cannot activate an engine version or become the universal evolution workflow.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine research owner

definition.normative_voice: A Research-Learning Cycle MUST preserve the typed progression from a research question through falsifiable hypothesis, experiment, observation, learning decision, and optional successor question.
definition.formal_voice: ResearchLearningCycle/v1 = Question -> Hypothesis -> Experiment -> Observation -> LearningDecision -> SuccessorQuestion?.
definition.plain_language_voice: This cycle turns uncertain questions into explicit learning without forcing every investigation to be a benchmark campaign.
definition.domain_context_voice: The existing research-learning ontology and research DAG provide its predecessor records and dependency model.
definition.boundary: An observation or learning decision does not create an engine variant, approve implementation, or authorize external research calls.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine research owner

definition.normative_voice: An Engine-Improvement Cycle MUST convert admitted improvement signals into a selected measurable target, candidate techniques, reproduced mechanisms, isolated engine variants, exact comparisons, and a recommend-only improvement decision.
definition.formal_voice: EngineImprovementCycle/v1 = Signals -> Target -> Techniques -> Reproductions -> Variants -> Comparisons -> RecommendationOrRejection.
definition.plain_language_voice: This cycle changes and compares the engine after evidence identifies something worth improving.
definition.domain_context_voice: It specializes the predecessor ARE EvolutionCycle while ending before activation.
definition.boundary: It does not own benchmark-research protocol history, serving activation, deployment, or unrestricted self-modification.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine product and implementation owners

definition.normative_voice: An Interaction-Learning Cycle MUST convert a bounded understanding assessment into a scoped lesson, declared application, observed application outcome, and improvement signal while preserving scope and counterevidence.
definition.formal_voice: InteractionLearningCycle/v1 = UnderstandingAssessment -> ScopedLesson -> LessonApplication -> ApplicationAssessment -> ImprovementSignal?.
definition.plain_language_voice: This cycle learns from how ARE and a user understood and applied information during real interactions.
definition.domain_context_voice: The existing interaction-learning implementation and ontology relationships supply its predecessor behavior.
definition.boundary: It does not generalize a preference globally, expose hidden reasoning, or directly change the engine.

concepts.decision_owner: Agent Reasoning Engine product-meaning owner plus interaction owner

definition.normative_voice: A Controlled-Upgrade Cycle MUST keep recommendation, owner authorization, exact predecessor binding, activation, canary observation, retention, and rollback as a separately governed lifecycle.
definition.formal_voice: ControlledUpgradeCycle/v1 = Recommendation -> AuthorizationGate -> Activate -> Canary -> Retain | Rollback | Block.
definition.plain_language_voice: This cycle controls whether a tested version actually becomes active and ensures it can be reversed.
definition.domain_context_voice: It extracts the existing upgrade-controller behavior from the engine-improvement cycle and preserves recommend-only defaults.
definition.boundary: A benchmark pass, comparison KEEP result, or runtime receipt cannot supply the missing owner authorization.

concepts.decision_owner: CyberAlchemy v2 effect owner plus Agent Reasoning Engine product and operations owners

source_refs.selector: verified dependency projection, topological layers, and informational research frontier
whole-cycle serialization and trigger replay behavior
research question, hypothesis, experiment, observation, and learning-decision records
fixed research contract, E0-E10 evolution cycle, H-EN queue, and round namespace
authority, provenance, durability, context, and candidate-definition terms

resolved_decisions.title: Cycle-definition admission
resolved_decisions.decision: Only the user may admit a new cycle definition, admit a successor version, accept a compatibility-breaking revision, or remove a definition from the active registry. Structural and compatibility validators may block malformed candidates but cannot approve them.
resolved_decisions.decided_in_request: route-020 followed by explicit approval in route-021
resolved_decisions.boundary: This records candidate architecture direction; it does not admit any current definition or authorize implementation.

resolved_decisions.title: Storage realization
resolved_decisions.decision: Use append-only event and receipt ledgers, a global content-addressed artifact store, and a transactional SQLite operational index that is fully rebuildable.
resolved_decisions.decided_in_request: route-020 followed by explicit approval in route-021
resolved_decisions.boundary: The exact codec, pack format, paths, thresholds, and implementation remain unselected.

resolved_decisions.title: Space-first evidence lifecycle
resolved_decisions.decision: Keep small identity, event, receipt, hash, accounting, decision, handoff, and archive metadata hot; deduplicate immutable bytes globally; compress warm objects; pack terminal, unpinned, unreferenced heavy data into verified cold archives; restore and verify original hashes before relying on an archive; garbage-collect only temporary or unreferenced disposable data automatically; require a separate user decision for permanent evidence deletion.
eligibility: no active lease references the data
the user has not pinned the data
no active cycle requires immediate access
a restoration check reproduces original content hashes
resolved_decisions.decided_in_request: route-020 followed by explicit approval in route-021
resolved_decisions.boundary: Archive is reversible storage movement, not deletion or weakening of evidence identity.

resolved_decisions.title: Artifact semantic validation
resolved_decisions.decision: The kernel validates command shape, bytes, hashes, schemas, provenance, and validator receipts. Each user-approved cycle definition pins its own semantic validators for evidence roles and transition criteria. Validators must be versioned, receipt-producing, fail closed, and rerun during recovery; agents and workers cannot assert evidence sufficiency directly.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Validators enforce the rules in a user-approved cycle definition; they do not admit definitions, establish external truth, grant authority, or approve effects.

resolved_decisions.title: Initial cycle registry scope
resolved_decisions.decision: The initial registry scope includes benchmark-research/v1, research-learning/v1, engine-improvement/v1, interaction-learning/v1, and controlled-upgrade/v1.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Registry scope is not definition admission or execution enablement. Each definition still requires the DG-01 user gate; controlled-upgrade remains non-activating until its separate authority and isolation gates pass.

resolved_decisions.title: Legacy benchmark import scope
resolved_decisions.decision: The first legacy import is limited to the evidence closure required to reconstruct the current GLM 8K ContextBench H-EN hypothesis and its current candidate as awaiting-validation, historically labeled E5, ready for independent construction review. The complete historical ContextBench campaign, ARE-DSH branch, older ContextBench work, and third benchmark remain outside the initial import.
preservation_requirements: missing evidence and receipts remain missing
new import receipt is dated at actual import
resolved_decisions.boundary: This selects migration scope only. It does not move files, synthesize history, admit the benchmark cycle, or authorize implementation or execution.

resolved_decisions.title: Controlled-upgrade isolation
resolved_decisions.decision: Controlled-upgrade/v1 shares the versioned JSON protocol and read access to explicitly handed-off evidence, but activation-capable execution runs in a separate process with separate credentials unavailable to research, benchmark, interaction-learning, and engine-improvement workers.
required_guards: exact serving predecessor and rollback target
activation credentials absent from non-upgrade processes
deterministic retain, rollback, or block settlement
resolved_decisions.boundary: Including controlled-upgrade/v1 in the registry does not start its process, provision credentials, authorize activation, deploy a variant, or grant any effect.

resolved_decisions.title: Benchmark-research cycle identity
resolved_decisions.decision: One benchmark-research cycle is identified and guided by one immutable improvement objective that binds the feature or capability being improved, goal, benchmark and cohort, metric policy, measured baseline, success and falsification conditions, and constraints. Candidate hypotheses and bounded attempts may vary within that lifecycle. A material objective change or untouched confirmation creates a linked successor cycle rather than mutating the original objective.
resolved_decisions.boundary: This defines cycle identity only. It does not admit an objective, classify H-EN and H-MC automatically, freeze a metric policy, import evidence, or authorize benchmark work.

resolved_decisions.title: Benchmark objective metric structure
resolved_decisions.decision: Every Benchmark Improvement Objective classifies its measures prospectively as primary metrics, guardrails, or diagnostic metrics and freezes an explicit decision rule. One or more primary metrics determine success through the declared logical rule; a guardrail blocks success when its frozen threshold is violated; diagnostics explain results but cannot alter the decision.
resolved_decisions.boundary: BR-02 does not select the actual metrics or thresholds for any benchmark objective, and it does not permit post-result metric reclassification.

resolved_decisions.title: Hypothesis organization inside a benchmark cycle
resolved_decisions.decision: One objective-bound benchmark-research cycle maintains an iterative portfolio of independently attributable hypotheses. Each hypothesis binds a falsifiable claim and mechanism and may produce multiple candidate implementations, experiments, and attempts. Evidence, accounting, freezes, execution identities, exposure, and outcomes remain attributable to the relevant hypothesis and candidate, while all records contribute to the same objective lifecycle.
isolation_requirements: no hypothesis may mutate the objective
evidence and accounting attributable to hypothesis, candidate, experiment, and attempt
explicit provenance and exposure posture for cross-hypothesis evidence reuse
resolved_decisions.boundary: A hypothesis, candidate, experiment, or attempt is a subordinate record, not a child cycle. It cannot mutate the objective, inherit another hypothesis's outcome, conceal exposure, or authorize execution.

resolved_decisions.title: Semantic benchmark lifecycle vocabulary
resolved_decisions.decision: Benchmark-research/v1 uses explicit semantic identifiers for commands, emitted events, and derived states. Numeric E0-E10 labels are prohibited as canonical runtime identifiers and may appear only as legacy aliases attached to imported historical evidence.

semantic_operations.projection_effect: restore the previously derived cycle and subordinate-record states; initialize awaiting-diagnosis only for a new cycle
record the objective gap and permit hypothesis registration
add one proposed hypothesis to the active portfolio
bind a prospective test to one hypothesis
record a terminal attempt and accounting
evaluate evidence under the frozen metric policy
support, revise, reject, or exhaust the hypothesis
complete, continue, stop, or cancel the objective lifecycle

resolved_decisions.boundary: A command proposes a transition, an event records an accepted fact, and a state is derived from events. Sharing a human-readable verb does not collapse these three identities or let a caller set state directly.

resolved_decisions.title: Objective-driven iterative hypothesis portfolio
resolved_decisions.decision: A benchmark-research cycle is one objective lifecycle. While it remains active, agents or admitted workers may propose as many falsifiable hypotheses as are useful and admissible within the cycle's declared budgets, concurrency, evidence, leakage, and safety constraints. Each hypothesis may yield multiple candidates, experiments, and attempts. The runtime registers, validates, accounts for, and derives status from those records; it does not create a separate child cycle for them.
resolved_decisions.boundary: There is no fixed schema-level hypothesis count, but 'as many as possible' does not bypass budgets, owner gates, concurrency, stop rules, or evidence requirements, and the runtime does not originate hypotheses autonomously.

resolved_decisions.title: Objective-cycle stopping and continuation
resolved_decisions.decision: The cycle continues while its immutable objective remains unmet, at least one admissible hypothesis or hypothesis-generation path remains, applicable resource ceilings permit more work, and no blocking prerequisite or user stop applies. Its derived disposition is determined by the frozen objective policy and recorded evidence rather than by an arbitrary hypothesis count.

cycle_dispositions.condition: the frozen success rule is satisfied at the objective's required evidence level and no guardrail blocks success
development criteria pass but the objective policy requires a separately frozen untouched confirmation successor
the objective is unmet and further admissible hypothesis work remains within all bounds
a temporary prerequisite, resource, or owner gate prevents progress without making the objective impossible
no admissible hypothesis or generation path remains, or a non-renewable hard resource ceiling is consumed before success
the user explicitly ends the cycle before another terminal disposition

resolved_decisions.boundary: A cycle disposition neither invents a new hypothesis nor authorizes provider calls, candidate construction, confirmation, activation, or any external effect. Paused is resumable; completed, confirmation-required, exhausted, and cancelled are terminal for the exact cycle.

resolved_decisions.title: Hypothesis proposal and admission
resolved_decisions.decision: An agent or admitted research worker may propose a hypothesis through the JSON protocol. The runtime registers it only after the bound cycle validator confirms objective relevance, a falsifiable claim, expected mechanism, explicit falsifier, novelty or declared predecessor revision, testability under the benchmark contract, expected evidence, resource estimate, provenance, exposure posture, and leakage, safety, and prohibited-method compliance.
admission_checks: distinct identity or explicit revision lineage
testability under the bound benchmark and cohort
declared resource estimate within remaining eligibility
resolved_decisions.boundary: Hypothesis admission makes a record eligible for prioritization only. It does not authorize construction, code mutation, provider calls, dispatch, benchmark execution, external effects, or objective completion, and the runtime does not originate the hypothesis.

resolved_decisions.title: Hypothesis priority and bounded work selection
resolved_decisions.decision: The runtime reuses the existing separation between the Research DAG and Research Work Plan. Verified records and explicit successor lineage produce an acyclic dependency projection; an immutable work plan declares tasks, owners, lanes, prerequisites, evidence criteria, and validators; event replay derives planned, ready, running, blocked, and completed states. The agent selects which derived-ready task to request next and supplies its rationale and resource request. The runtime enforces current state, dependencies, expected revision, budget, concurrency, effect gates, and evidence-bound completion.
existing_contract_alignment: the DAG frontier is informational and grants no scheduling readiness
ready is derived from the immutable work plan and accepted events
independent ready branches remain available when another branch blocks
events are replayable and idempotent while conflicts and stale state fail
the generic scheduler serializes whole-cycle triggers and is not a hypothesis-ranking engine
resolved_decisions.validation_evidence: On 2026-09-20, the focused research-dag, research-work, and operations test files passed 21 of 21 tests.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The agent's priority choice does not set readiness or state. A ready task is not automatically dispatched, and neither the DAG, work plan, frontier, nor scheduler grants permission for construction, provider calls, benchmark execution, or another external effect.

resolved_decisions.title: Benchmark comparison-reference mode
resolved_decisions.decision: Every Benchmark Improvement Objective prospectively selects exactly one comparison-reference mode: absolute-target, frozen-baseline, or prospective-paired-control. The selected mode, exact reference evidence, compatible metric policy, and permitted claim language become immutable parts of the objective. Benchmark-research/v1 does not universally require or universally forbid a fresh control.

reference_modes.meaning: Evaluate candidates against prospectively frozen absolute thresholds without claiming relative improvement over a newly measured control.
Compare candidates with exact pre-existing baseline evidence whose provenance, age, compatibility, and claim ceiling are frozen in the objective.
Run candidate and control under one prospectively frozen matched contract and account for both arms.

resolved_decisions.current_glm8k_binding: The current GLM 8K ContextBench objective uses frozen-baseline mode with candidate-only new calls. Historical controls remain descriptive evidence; they do not newly establish a matched efficiency claim.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Changing reference mode, reference evidence, or the claims permitted by that mode creates a successor objective cycle. This decision does not select a mode for unrelated future cycles or authorize any control or candidate calls.

resolved_decisions.title: Experiment freeze, successor, and attempt identity
resolved_decisions.decision: An experiment remains editable only while draft. Before any measurement-bearing execution, it freezes the exact hypothesis, candidate and implementation bytes, model and reasoning settings, benchmark and cohort, prompts and context policy, metrics and decision rule, source and leakage policy, budgets, stop conditions, retry policy, concurrency, adapters, validators, and configuration. Every execution is a separately identified and settled attempt under that exact frozen experiment. Any post-freeze contract change creates a content-addressed successor experiment linked to its predecessor.
resolved_decisions.retry_rule: A retry is admissible only when the frozen experiment policy permits it. Each failed, partial, timed-out, cancelled, or successful attempt remains visible with its evidence and known or unknown accounting; no automatic retry may be invented after failure.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Freezing proves configuration identity and prospective ordering only. It does not authorize execution, establish that an attempt occurred, validate its evidence, or permit post-result changes under the original experiment identity.

resolved_decisions.title: Evidence-bound hypothesis decision outcomes
resolved_decisions.decision: A hypothesis decision is derived from verified experiment and observation evidence and uses only the declared typed outcomes. Nonterminal outcomes request replication, another experiment, or a successor revision. Terminal outcomes support, reject, or exhaust the exact hypothesis. Inconclusive preserves uncertainty and may remain nonterminal while another admissible test exists.

outcomes.meaning: More independent observations under the declared replication rule are required.
A declared experiment remains necessary and admissible.
Close the exact hypothesis and create an explicitly linked successor rather than mutate it.
Verified evidence satisfies the frozen support criteria without satisfying the falsifier.
Verified evidence satisfies the frozen falsifier or rejection rule.
Current evidence cannot decide; continue only if another admissible evidence path exists.
The hypothesis remains unsupported and undecided but no admissible test remains within the cycle bounds.

resolved_decisions.compatibility: Existing candidate-supported learning decisions import as the canonical supported outcome while preserving their original bytes and vocabulary as legacy evidence.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The agent may request a decision but cannot assert its outcome. Supported does not by itself complete the objective, retain an engine change, authorize confirmation, or activate a candidate.

resolved_decisions.title: Cycle execution envelope and experiment launch admission
resolved_decisions.decision: The user authorizes one immutable bounded execution envelope for the objective cycle. It declares allowed providers and models, credential slots, data classifications and exposure, experiment classes, maximum calls, tokens, cost, elapsed time, concurrency, applicable geography and network constraints, and expiry. Each frozen experiment requires a runtime launch-admission receipt proving that it is wholly inside the active envelope and that its declared prerequisites pass. Once admitted, permitted attempts and frozen-policy retries may dispatch without repeated user approval.
resolved_decisions.out_of_envelope_rule: Any requested provider, model, credential use, data exposure, resource quantity, experiment class, or effect outside the envelope blocks and requires a new explicit user decision. Neither the runtime nor an agent may expand the envelope.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Envelope authorization is not cycle-definition admission, proof that launch prerequisites passed, or activation or deployment authority. Experiment freeze, validation, launch admission, dispatch lease, attempt, and settlement remain distinct records.

resolved_decisions.title: Conditional independent-agent evaluation and validation
resolved_decisions.decision: Deterministic validators are the normal validation path. When a result needs additional evaluation, the runtime creates a typed review task and sends the exact output plus its immutable evidence bundle to a different agent. That evaluation agent checks the output against the frozen experiment, metrics, evidence, claim ceiling, and applicable policies, then returns a structured recommendation and validation receipt to the runtime.
review_triggers: a validator fails, returns unknown, or reports ambiguity
the output is novel or materially different from conditions covered by the frozen rules
evidence, accounting, provenance, or leakage status is missing or uncertain
the proposed conclusion would exceed the declared claim ceiling
resolved_decisions.separation_rule: The evaluation agent must be distinct from the agent that produced or selected the reviewed output and receives a runtime-assembled evidence bundle rather than mutable cycle state. Its identity, role, inputs, outputs, and model or policy configuration are recorded.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The evaluation agent advises and validates; it cannot mutate cycle state, widen the experiment or execution envelope, assert a hypothesis outcome, or grant authority. The runtime applies deterministic transition rules. A user decision remains required when review exposes an unresolved authority boundary, an out-of-envelope action, or a material definition change.

resolved_decisions.title: Research-learning cycle identity and guiding objective
resolved_decisions.decision: One research-learning/v1 cycle is identified and guided by one immutable bounded research question together with its intended learning outcome and declared use. The cycle may contain multiple falsifiable hypotheses, experiments, observations, and learning decisions that contribute to answering that question.
resolved_decisions.successor_rule: A material change to the research question, intended learning outcome, declared use, scope, or answerability criteria creates an explicitly linked successor cycle rather than mutating the original identity.
resolved_decisions.boundary: A hypothesis, experiment, observation, or technique candidate is subordinate evidence or output and does not identify a separate cycle merely by existing. The question does not authorize research calls, implementation, retention, activation, publication, or deployment.

resolved_decisions.title: Evidence-derived research-question disposition
resolved_decisions.decision: The runtime derives the research question's disposition from the complete verified evidence portfolio rather than from any single supported hypothesis or proposed technique. Every disposition records the answer or unresolved portion, evidence strength or confidence, supporting evidence, counterevidence, limitations, applicability boundary, and any successor question.

dispositions.meaning: The frozen answerability criteria are satisfied for the declared use.
A bounded subset is answered and the record explicitly preserves the unanswered portion and why the cycle closes.
The current evidence cannot answer the question; research may continue only while another admissible path remains.
The question remains unanswered or inconclusive and no admissible evidence path remains within the cycle bounds.
The question's assumptions, referents, or answerability conditions are shown to be invalid; a materially corrected question requires a successor cycle.

resolved_decisions.boundary: A supported hypothesis contributes evidence but cannot by itself answer the cycle question. A technique candidate is an optional handoff, not a completion requirement. No disposition grants implementation, retention, activation, publication, or deployment authority.

resolved_decisions.title: Prospectively frozen answerability contract
resolved_decisions.decision: Before cycle admission, the research question binds an immutable answerability contract. The contract declares acceptable evidence classes and provenance quality, minimum sufficiency and any independence requirements, counterevidence treatment, confidence or evidence-strength semantics, applicability boundaries, resource ceilings, and stopping, exhaustion, and invalidation conditions. The admitted contract is content-addressed and applies to every later question disposition.
resolved_decisions.change_rule: Additional evidence may be admitted when it conforms to the frozen contract. A material change to sufficiency, confidence, applicability, evidence classes, counterevidence handling, resources, or stopping conditions creates an explicitly linked successor cycle rather than revising the active threshold after results are known.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The answerability contract is a prospective decision rule, not evidence that the question has been answered and not authorization to acquire evidence, spend resources, call providers, implement changes, or publish conclusions.

resolved_decisions.title: Typed multimodal research evidence
resolved_decisions.decision: A research-learning cycle may admit typed source or literature analysis, repository or static-code inspection, existing verified artifacts, observational evidence, reproductions, controlled experiments, benchmark results, and structured evaluation-agent reviews when the frozen answerability contract permits the exact mode. Controlled experiments may be mandatory for a particular question but are not universal to research learning.
resolved_decisions.evidence_requirements: Every evidence item binds immutable source bytes or an exact external reference snapshot, evidence type, acquisition method, provenance, quality posture, independence posture, temporal scope, limitations, applicability, claim ceiling, validator identity, and verification receipt. Derived claims retain links to all contributing evidence and counterevidence.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Evidence modes are not interchangeable merely because they address the same question. Agent notes without typed provenance and validation are proposals, not admitted evidence. Evidence admission does not authorize acquisition effects or elevate a claim beyond its weakest required supporting source.

resolved_decisions.title: Structured non-authorizing research finding handoff
resolved_decisions.decision: A research-learning cycle may export an immutable Research Finding Bundle containing the exact research question and disposition, supported, rejected, and unresolved hypotheses, evidence and counterevidence, confidence or evidence strength, limitations, applicability boundaries, claim ceiling, suggested successor questions, optional technique candidates, complete provenance, and validation receipts.
resolved_decisions.acceptance_rule: A receiving cycle must explicitly accept the exact bundle digest and declare which claims and optional candidates it adopts for its own bounded objective. Rejection or partial acceptance leaves the source bundle unchanged and is recorded by the receiver.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The handoff transfers immutable evidence and bounded claims only. It does not transfer cycle state, budgets, credentials, permissions, ownership, implementation admission, retention, activation, publication, or deployment authority.

resolved_decisions.title: Derived readiness, agent selection, and runtime launch admission
resolved_decisions.decision: The immutable Research Work Plan and Research DAG derive ready work from exact record versions and satisfied dependencies. A research agent selects among ready tasks. Before dispatch, the runtime verifies the expected plan and state revision, prerequisites, task criteria, budgets, concurrency, effect policy, and lease availability, then issues a launch-admission receipt for work inside the user-approved research-learning execution envelope.
resolved_decisions.execution_rule: The cycle envelope bounds providers and models, credential slots, data exposure, evidence-acquisition classes, calls, tokens, cost, time, concurrency, retries, and expiry. Admitted in-policy work and frozen-policy retries may proceed without repeated user approval. Out-of-envelope work blocks and requires a new user decision. Recovery replays recorded events and settles or expires leases before redispatch.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The DAG expresses dependency order and readiness but is not a dispatcher. Agent selection cannot bypass runtime admission, and runtime admission cannot widen the envelope, answer the research question, implement a technique, or transfer authority.

resolved_decisions.title: Engine-improvement cycle identity and guiding objective
resolved_decisions.decision: One engine-improvement/v1 cycle is identified and guided by one immutable measurable improvement objective. The objective binds accepted improvement signals or research findings, the exact engine surface, desired behavior, primary and guardrail metrics, exact baseline identity, scope, prohibited changes, resource limits, and stopping bounds. Multiple technique candidates, reproduction trials, implementation attempts, and content-addressed engine variants may compete beneath that objective.
resolved_decisions.successor_rule: A material change to the accepted inputs, engine surface, desired behavior, metrics, baseline, scope, prohibited changes, or bounds creates an explicitly linked successor cycle rather than mutating the active objective.
resolved_decisions.boundary: A technique candidate, engine variant, or code branch is subordinate work and does not identify the cycle. Objective admission does not authorize mutation, comparison execution, retention, activation, publication, release, or deployment.

resolved_decisions.title: Recommend-only typed improvement decision
resolved_decisions.decision: Verified reproduction and comparison evidence yields only typed improvement decisions: recommend-variant, reject-variant, revise-technique, continue-comparison, or exhausted. A recommendation binds the exact content-addressed variant bytes, exact baseline and environment, comparison protocol and results, primary and guardrail outcomes, limitations, applicability, rollback requirements, evidence digests, and validation receipts.
resolved_decisions.disposition_rule: Rejecting a variant, revising a technique, or continuing comparison may leave the objective cycle active while an admissible portfolio path remains. The cycle completes with a recommend-variant decision when its frozen selection rule is satisfied, or exhausted when no admissible path remains within the objective bounds.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Every decision is advisory and non-activating. A recommendation may be offered to a separately admitted controlled-upgrade cycle but cannot change the serving pointer, merge itself, publish itself, or grant any downstream authority.

resolved_decisions.title: Content-addressed isolated variant construction
resolved_decisions.decision: Each engine variant is constructed in an isolated workspace outside the serving checkout. Its construction contract binds the exact baseline commit and selected source bytes, dependencies, toolchain, environment, mutation allowlist, prohibited paths, technique candidate, builder identity, and one runtime-controlled writer lease. Commands, file changes, validator results, and settlements produce receipts.
resolved_decisions.identity_rule: Before measurement, the runtime seals the complete variant bytes and construction bindings into a content-addressed variant identity. Any later byte or binding change creates an explicitly linked successor variant. No result measured against one identity may be attributed to another.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The isolated workspace cannot modify serving state, escape the mutation allowlist, inherit undeclared credentials, or share an uncontrolled writer. Construction identity and isolation do not prove correctness or authorize comparison, retention, activation, or downstream effects.

resolved_decisions.title: Frozen staged portfolio comparison and selection
resolved_decisions.decision: Before variant results are visible, the cycle freezes a staged comparison contract binding exact baseline and variant identities, screening cohort and metrics, advancement thresholds, full-evaluation repetitions, guardrails and failure rules, independent confirmation cohort, aggregation and tie-breaking rules, final selection criteria, budgets, retry policy, and stopping conditions. All branches, attempts, failures, and eliminations remain recorded.
resolved_decisions.selection_rule: A variant may be recommended only after passing every required stage and guardrail under the frozen contract. Screening may allocate additional evaluation only according to the prospective advancement rule. Missing confirmation remains explicit and limits the recommendation rather than being silently treated as success.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The agent cannot change cohorts, metrics, thresholds, aggregation, or selection rules after observing results. A material comparison-contract change creates a successor comparison, and a winning comparison remains recommend-only.

resolved_decisions.title: Exact retention with recomputed currentness
resolved_decisions.decision: An Improvement Retention record binds one exact implemented-and-verified candidate identity to the content-addressed variant, selected implementation source or configuration paths, objective and baseline identities, comparison and confirmation evidence, validators, toolchain, limitations, applicability, and all selected dependency digests. It may suppress rediscovery only while every selected binding remains current.
resolved_decisions.currentness_rule: The runtime recomputes currentness whenever retention is considered. A missing or changed selected implementation, configuration, toolchain, validator, baseline, or evidence binding marks the retention stale and returns the exact candidate to the experiment frontier. Historical retention and evidence records remain immutable and visible.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Retention is exact duplicate suppression and provenance, not permanent truth. It cannot suppress a materially different candidate and grants no serving, activation, publication, or downstream authority.

resolved_decisions.title: Bounded effect envelope with construction and comparison admission
resolved_decisions.decision: The user approves one immutable bounded engine-improvement effect envelope declaring mutation scopes and allowed command classes, toolchains, builds, tests, containers, network and provider access, credential slots, data exposure, maximum workspaces, calls, tokens, cost, elapsed time, concurrency, retries, recovery policy, and expiry. The runtime issues a construction-admission receipt before an isolated workspace may be mutated and a separate comparison-admission receipt before measurement begins against frozen variant bytes.
resolved_decisions.execution_rule: In-policy construction, validation, comparison, and frozen-policy retries may proceed without repeated user approval after their required admission. Any new mutation scope, command class, provider, credential use, data exposure, resource amount, or effect outside the envelope blocks and requires a new explicit user decision.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The envelope and admission receipts authorize only bounded cycle effects. They do not change variant identity, waive validators or frozen comparison rules, make a recommendation authoritative, or permit changes to active state.

resolved_decisions.title: Interaction-learning cycle identity and scoped objective
resolved_decisions.decision: One interaction-learning/v1 cycle is identified and guided by one immutable scoped learning objective. The objective binds the attributed understanding or interaction problem, subject and context scope, intended participant or interaction cohort, desired interaction behavior, primary and guardrail criteria, privacy and consent posture, data-retention and revocation boundaries, resource limits, and stopping conditions. Multiple scoped lessons, applications, and application assessments may contribute beneath that objective.
resolved_decisions.successor_rule: A material change to the observed problem, subject, cohort, desired behavior, criteria, privacy or consent posture, retention boundary, or resource bounds creates an explicitly linked successor cycle rather than widening the current lesson scope.
resolved_decisions.boundary: An individual conversation, turn, correction, or inferred preference is subordinate evidence and does not identify the cycle. Objective admission does not establish semantic understanding, authorize global personalization, expose hidden reasoning, or change the engine.

resolved_decisions.title: Attributed, minimized, policy-eligible interaction evidence
resolved_decisions.decision: An interaction-learning/v1 cycle may admit explicit user corrections and approvals, observable task outcomes, deterministic checks, and scoped lesson-application outcomes only when each evidence item carries source attribution, subject and context scope, consent or other declared policy basis, data classification, minimization or redaction treatment, retention and expiry, revocation handling, limitations, and a validator receipt. Raw interaction content is referenced by stable binding or retained in the minimum redacted form necessary for the declared objective rather than copied wholesale by default.
resolved_decisions.exclusions: Hidden chain-of-thought, secrets, unauthorized third-party private content, unverified inference, and model self-assessment are not admissible learning evidence. An inferred preference remains a proposal until attributable validation, and evidence from one participant or cohort cannot be generalized outside its declared scope.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Evidence admission establishes provenance and policy eligibility only. It does not prove a lesson, authorize application, override current user instructions, expand personalization scope, or permit retention after expiry or revocation.

resolved_decisions.title: Evidence-supported lesson derivation and scope-matched application
resolved_decisions.decision: A scoped lesson may be derived only when its admitted evidence portfolio satisfies the interaction objective's declared sufficiency and guardrail criteria. Before every application, the runtime deterministically matches the lesson's subject, participant or cohort, context, purpose, privacy posture, and validity interval against the current interaction. A current explicit user instruction always takes precedence. Every attempted application produces an evidence-bound outcome receipt, including a no-application result when matching or policy checks fail.
resolved_decisions.lifecycle_rule: Expiry or revocation immediately makes the lesson ineligible for new applications. Historical derivation and application receipts remain immutable evidence subject to their own retention policy, while any reusable content whose retention authority ended must be removed or rendered inaccessible according to the recorded revocation treatment.
resolved_decisions.boundary: A supported lesson is neither a global rule nor authority to override current instructions, policy, privacy boundaries, or another participant's scope. Application evidence may inform later lesson assessment but cannot silently widen applicability or modify the engine.

resolved_decisions.title: Typed application outcomes and bounded recurrence
resolved_decisions.decision: Every scope-matched lesson application receives one typed outcome: confirmed, ineffective, harmful, inconclusive, or not-applicable. The runtime derives lesson standing from the complete admitted evidence portfolio as candidate, supported, contested, suspended, revoked, or expired; the latest result cannot overwrite prior evidence. Objective success requires the prospectively declared recurrence or independent-replication threshold with no blocking guardrail failure.
resolved_decisions.terminal_rule: Contradiction and guardrail evidence is retained and may deterministically revise, contest, suspend, or revoke a lesson under the declared rule. The cycle terminates only with one evidence-bound disposition: achieved, partially-achieved, exhausted, revoked, or superseded. Each disposition binds the evaluated portfolio, thresholds, unmet criteria, limitations, and decision receipt.
resolved_decisions.boundary: A favorable application does not by itself establish durable improvement, and terminal cycle status does not authorize persistent memory, prompt or policy changes, engine mutation, upgrade, deployment, or cross-scope reuse.

resolved_decisions.title: Bounded interaction operation and non-authorizing handoff
resolved_decisions.decision: One immutable user-approved interaction-learning effect envelope bounds evidence capture, data exposure and classification, retention, lesson application modes, participant or cohort scope, privacy and consent posture, resources, expiry, revocation, and stop conditions. The runtime requires the applicable admission before evidence capture or retention and before live lesson application. Completion emits an immutable Interaction Learning Bundle binding the objective, scoped lessons, evidence digests, application and assessment receipts, lesson standing, terminal disposition, limitations, applicability, retention, expiry, and revocation rules.
resolved_decisions.handoff_rule: The cycle may offer its bundle or a derived non-authorizing improvement signal to another cycle. A receiving cycle must explicitly validate and accept the exact handoff under its own definition and envelope. Persistent-memory, prompt, policy, engine, activation, release, or deployment changes require their separately owned admission and cannot be inferred from lesson support or cycle completion.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The envelope authorizes only its exact bounded interaction-learning operations. The bundle transfers evidence and scoped claims, never state, credentials, permissions, ownership, implementation authority, or downstream effect authority.

resolved_decisions.title: Minimal immutable controlled-upgrade identity
resolved_decisions.decision: One controlled-upgrade/v1 cycle is identified by a minimal immutable Activation Binding containing the exact content-addressed candidate, the target serving environment or slot, and the exact serving predecessor that is also the rollback point. The source recommendation remains linked evidence. Owner authorization is a separate receipt over the digest of this binding.
resolved_decisions.successor_rule: Changing the candidate, target, or serving predecessor creates a successor cycle and invalidates reuse of the earlier authorization. Canary rules, budgets, schedules, credentials, and other execution details remain separately bound operational records rather than fields that enlarge cycle identity.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The Activation Binding coordinates only the minimum identities needed to prevent candidate, target, predecessor, or authorization substitution. Creating it does not authorize activation, provision credentials, or approve any operational policy.

resolved_decisions.title: One human authorization boundary
resolved_decisions.decision: After deterministic readiness checks pass, the user provides one authorization receipt over the exact Activation Binding and its separately bound execution policy. The isolated upgrade controller may then activate the candidate, observe the bounded canary, and deterministically retain or roll back without additional human approvals.
resolved_decisions.deviation_rule: The controller must block and return to the user before proceeding when the binding or policy has changed, readiness no longer holds, a required action is outside the approved policy, or deterministic settlement is impossible. An emergency rollback to the already approved rollback point does not require another approval.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The single approval applies only to the exact binding and bounded policy. It cannot be reused for a successor cycle, another target, a different predecessor, broader credentials, or an unbounded operational action.

resolved_decisions.title: Minimum final activation readiness invariant
resolved_decisions.decision: Immediately before activation, the isolated controller deterministically verifies only that the candidate bytes match the approved Activation Binding, the target still serves the bound predecessor, the rollback point is available, and the authorization plus execution policy remain current. Any failed or indeterminate check blocks activation.
resolved_decisions.switch_rule: The serving change is conditional on an atomic comparison with the expected predecessor. A concurrent or otherwise unexplained serving-state change fails the comparison and produces a blocked receipt rather than overwriting the new state.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Readiness proves only that the exact approved change can begin from the expected recoverable state. It does not prove canary success, authorize a different target or candidate, or permit best-effort activation after missing evidence.

resolved_decisions.title: Deterministic fail-closed canary settlement
resolved_decisions.decision: The separately bound execution policy freezes the canary signals, thresholds, observation window, and deadline before activation. A passing result retains the candidate. A failed result, missing required evidence, or an inconclusive result at the deadline triggers automatic rollback to the bound predecessor. Every result produces an evidence-bound settlement receipt.
resolved_decisions.failure_rule: Rollback uses the already approved recovery path and requires no new routine approval. If rollback cannot be verified, the controller enters blocked state, preserves the observed serving state and evidence without claiming recovery, and alerts the user for an exceptional decision.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The controller cannot retain by absence of evidence, change thresholds after observing results, extend the deadline outside policy, or let an evaluation agent replace the deterministic settlement rule.

resolved_decisions.title: Journal replay and observed-state reconciliation
resolved_decisions.decision: After interruption, the isolated controller replays the durable journal and reads the actual serving state before issuing any effect. If the predecessor is active, activation is not considered completed and may resume only through the normal final readiness check. If the candidate is active while policy remains valid, canary observation resumes from the recorded boundary without resetting its window. If the candidate is active after policy expiry, rollback begins. Any other or unverifiable serving state blocks and alerts the user.
resolved_decisions.idempotency_rule: Recovery commands and serving transitions carry stable operation identities. Replaying an already completed operation returns its prior receipt rather than repeating the effect, and every reconciliation produces a recovery receipt binding journal position, observed state, chosen action, and resulting state.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Recovery cannot infer retention, reset a canary window, overwrite unknown serving state, change the Activation Binding, or expand authorization. Unknown or contradictory evidence remains blocked for an exceptional user decision.

resolved_decisions.title: Cross-cycle consistency review before implementation planning
