resolved_decisions.decision: Perform a bounded cross-cycle consistency and implementation-readiness review before entering a separately routed implementation-planning phase. The review checks state ownership, handoff and authority boundaries, duplicated mechanisms, recovery semantics, predecessor-runtime alignment, and avoidable coordination complexity.
resolved_decisions.review_evidence: The existing predecessor evolution-runtime test suite passed 54 of 54 tests during route-033. The five cycle identities and non-authorizing handoffs are mutually compatible, but the documents do not yet unambiguously separate aggregate cycle state from subordinate hypothesis, experiment, attempt, lesson, variant, and work-item state.
resolved_decisions.boundary: The review may identify and clarify candidate semantics. It does not create an implementation plan, admit a definition, authorize construction, or claim that the predecessor runtime implements the candidate architecture.

resolved_decisions.title: Layered state projections from one event authority
resolved_decisions.decision: One authoritative verified event chain derives three non-competing projection layers: aggregate cycle state for the objective-level disposition; subordinate record state for hypotheses, questions, experiments, attempts, lessons, variants, comparisons, and upgrade records; and executable work state for planned, ready, running, blocked, expired, or settled work items. Semantic operations address the appropriate record or work item and then recompute all affected projections.
resolved_decisions.coordination_rule: Independent hypotheses and work items may progress concurrently while the aggregate cycle remains active. A subordinate terminal result contributes evidence to the objective rule but cannot directly set the aggregate cycle disposition. Every inspection view returns the three layers together with their source event revision so no layer becomes a second authority.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Layering is a projection distinction, not separate ledgers, mutable status stores, child cycles, or permission for components to own state independently.

resolved_decisions.title: Shared kernel envelope and admission mechanism
resolved_decisions.decision: The evolution kernel implements one generic envelope and admission mechanism for immutable policy identity, scope, bounded effects, resource ceilings, credential-slot references, data exposure, validity and expiry, currentness, prerequisite checks, admission receipts, deviations, and recovery. Cycle definitions supply typed policy fields, semantic validators, and named admission phases such as experiment launch, construction, comparison, evidence capture, lesson application, and activation.
resolved_decisions.coordination_rule: The shared mechanism evaluates the exact cycle-defined policy and requested phase without interpreting scientific or product meaning. One envelope may support multiple named admissions when the cycle definition permits it, but an admission for one phase, cycle, or binding cannot be reused for another.
resolved_decisions.boundary: Sharing admission mechanics does not merge cycle policies, budgets, credentials, authority owners, or receipts. The kernel cannot invent allowed effects or use generic admission to bypass cycle-specific validators or user authorization.

resolved_decisions.title: Enter a separately routed implementation-planning phase
resolved_decisions.decision: Move the reviewed candidate architecture into a separately routed implementation-planning phase that defines bounded construction slices, dependencies, validation strategy, operational support, and benchmark-resumption prerequisites.
resolved_decisions.planning_evidence: CA2-ROUTE-PLAN request route-037 produced goals/projects/agent-reasoning-engine/plans/multi-cycle-evolution-runtime/PLAN.md and IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.v1-candidate.json as candidate planning artifacts.

resolved_decisions.boundary: Selecting planning does not promote this Definition Pack, admit a Goal or cycle definition, authorize construction, migrate evidence, resume a benchmark, call a provider, activate a variant, or grant any external effect.

checks.detail: All thirty-one required concepts have exactly one candidate disposition, owner, boundary, and source binding.
Generic coordination and evidence mechanics are separated from cycle-specific states, transitions, criteria, budgets, and terminal outcomes.
Benchmark research, research learning, engine improvement, interaction learning, and controlled upgrade are separately defined.
Commands, events, artifacts, bindings, receipts, accounting, projections, reconstruction, and legacy import are explicitly modeled.
Agents and adapters submit commands; only deterministic runtime reduction produces cycle state.
Cross-cycle handoffs carry typed evidence and claim ceilings but never transfer state or authority automatically.

DG-01 through DG-07 preserve the user's admission boundary, hybrid space-first storage, cycle-specific validation, all-five registry scope, bounded H-EN-first import, and isolated controlled upgrade without claiming admission, implementation, migration, execution, activation, or deployment.
All seven presented cross-cycle architecture gates are resolved; the subsequent per-cycle definition audit does not reopen them unless contradictory evidence appears.

BR-08 preserves the tested separation between dependency projection, derived work readiness, caller-selected ready work, evidence-bound completion, and non-authorizing whole-cycle serialization; 21 focused tests passed on 2026-09-20.

The currently identified definition gates are closed for benchmark-research/v1, research-learning/v1, engine-improvement/v1, interaction-learning/v1, and controlled-upgrade/v1. CU-05 adds deterministic, idempotent interruption recovery. This is candidate semantic readiness only and does not admit implementation or any cycle definition.

The bounded NX-01 review found coherent cycle identities, storage, handoff, recovery, and authority boundaries, and the predecessor evolution-runtime passed 54 of 54 tests. CR-01 establishes layered projections under one event authority and CR-02 establishes one shared kernel admission mechanism with cycle-specific policy. Exact schemas, validators, storage layout, migration, and predecessor gaps remain downstream planning work; this PASS grants no implementation or admission authority.
The pack authorizes no implementation, migration, provider use, benchmark dispatch, activation, publication, release, or deployment.

allowed_uses: Review and challenge the proposed multi-cycle evolution vocabulary.
